HOW TO USE THIS FOR THE HEALTHCARE-ATTITUDES STUDY

Detail: foreign_nationals_pct_pop - the share of residents who are non-nationals. This is the population actually at issue in "publicly funded healthcare for non-nationals", it covers 35 of 40 countries, and every value is graded A or B.
foreign_born_pct_pop - wider coverage (38 countries) but it includes naturalised citizens, who are nationals and therefore not the group the survey question is about.

Do NOT use as a continuous cross-national regressor. Coverage is 11.0% of the 2010-2022 country-years for stocks (not collected earlier), the methods are not comparable, and detections are a flow driven by enforcement intensity. Use at most as an ordinal salience indicator, or restrict to within-country variation.

Dates differ by source and are recorded per value (*_ref_date). Eurostat stocks are 1 January of the labelled year; OECD dates follow the national source (30 June for Australia's foreign-born, 1 January for the foreign population of Japan, Turkey, the United Kingdom and Germany, none stated for several survey- or census-based series). Years are as the publisher labels them and nothing was shifted. If the survey is fielded mid-year, either lag the covariate or state the convention explicitly.
population (World Bank) and population_un_wpp2024 are both supplied. Choose one and use it throughout; they differ by more than 3% for 30 country-years.
